Help Lightning’s patented technology uses Merged Reality to combine two real-time video streams into a collaborative work environment shared between a remote expert and an on-site technician.

Ricoh is a global technology company with an entrepreneurial spirit. Since its founding in 1936, the company launched the first generation of fax machines and has since transitioned into digital copiers and other collaboration tools and hardware.

Though hardware is a critical part of Ricoh’s legacy, its next evolutionary step was to transition from a hardware-centric enterprise to one focused on high-quality service and customer experience. This would include adoption of more sophisticated technologies, both physical and digital.

An analysis found that customers’ print volumes were decreasing 30% year over year. As customers increasingly used digital tools for information exchange, Ricoh’s need for primarily hardware-oriented technicians declined.

The company set out to reshape its service teams for customers’ new needs. It asked, “What if we trained our teams to provide IT-related services?” Each technician already had some level of IT industry certification and substantial customer service experience. Transforming the service organization would require additional certifications and a new range of service-oriented digital technologies.

Ricoh also re-engineered the support process for technicians, moving beyond the traditional practice of calling a centralized help desk far from the job site. In the past, an operator might not have been a functional expert and could put technicians on hold while gathering resources, delaying repairs and inconveniencing customers.
The new process would connect technicians with the right resources at the right time and in the right context. Help Lightning became a central part of that process.

Ricoh gave its hardware-trained technicians the opportunity to become fully trained and certified in IT. The new approach combined reactive IT support, scheduled office support, and a hybrid of the two using Help Lightning’s Merged Reality.
These business units created value for customers through improved service and illustrated Ricoh’s commitment to leading-edge technologies.

“The key message to our clients is, we understand what their ROI targets are,” says Edward Krzysik, Director, Service Programs at Ricoh. “If we can put in the right resources, technology, processes, and best practices, we can help them achieve ROI at a much faster pace.”
1990 — Introduced the fastest digital color printer at 15 pages per minute.
2018 — Introduced Ricoh’s Print Platform Cloud Service.

Ricoh’s process begins with technicians in the field. A technician launches a service call through an app, Twitter, text, or phone. The call enters a queue in Ricoh Express Support, the company’s centralized business group.
Team members select service calls based on their experience and functional expertise. Each call goes to the person best equipped to handle that technology or product for the customer.

Silver Tsunami - Customer Case Study

Silver Tsunami, a field-service company confronting the industry “silver tsunami” of retiring technicians, faced shrinking on-site expertise, rising training costs, longer downtimes, and falling first-time fix rates. To bridge the gap, they adopted Help Lightning’s virtual expertise software (Virtual Expertise) to connect inexperienced field techs with senior experts remotely.

Help Lightning’s Virtual Expertise let remote experts guide new technicians in real time, cutting initial training from four months to six weeks (a 62.5% reduction), enabling same-day fixes, improving uptime and first-time fix rates, and boosting customer satisfaction while extending workforce capacity and reducing training-related opportunity costs.

Already well known for hardware, Ricoh has transitioned into a service-led business model. The company sought new business lines and revenue-generating opportunities that would support this services transformation.

Ricoh’s innovations in service delivery are part of a strategy called “The Ricoh Way.” In June 2019, Ricoh partnered with Help Lightning to address four main points of this strategy: innovation in service delivery; “What if?”; innovation — The Ricoh Way; and transformation through strategic partnerships.

Help Lightning made Ricoh personnel’s transition to the new technology easy. Global company uses Help Lightning to deliver customer support that saves costs, increases revenue, and delivers greater value to customers.

Dan Turner is Global Service Business Manager at Oxford Instruments NanoAnalysis. His team uses Help Lightning to provide remote expert guidance through a service it calls Live Assist. He shares how the team adds value to its support model while growing revenue.

“Customers think it’s otherworldly when they see the images projected in 3D right on their screen. It’s a greater level of intimacy compared to a phone call or email, and that translates to a minimal time to repair. There is no more guesswork. If an engineer must go on site, they are able to fix the issue in one visit. That gives customers maximum uptime, and that’s more revenue for the customer.”
Boost Revenue While Adding Value

Remote expert guidance with Help Lightning enables Oxford Instruments to serve more customers faster while reducing travel and engineer downtime. With the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, call volumes through Live Assist surged, translating to a 19% increase in revenue.

Help Lightning powers the Live Assist remote expert guidance service for Oxford Instruments NanoAnalysis, enabling the company to provide better, faster support while increasing revenue at higher margins.
